mechanics.mechanic: Open by defining the topic in plain language, then preview the main explanatory system and the practical decisions the audience will be able to make. This creates a clear contract between theory and application.
mechanics.when_to_use: Use when a subject is technical or spans several interacting domains.
mechanics.avoid: Do not promise more certainty or practical control than the explanation can support.

mechanics.mechanic: Introduce the system in successive layers: begin with a broad control center, add a second subsystem, then show how signals circulate between them. Each layer should answer what it does before explaining how it interacts with the others.
mechanics.when_to_use: Use for biology, technology, policy, or any topic involving distributed causes rather than a single mechanism.
mechanics.avoid: Do not introduce specialized components before giving the audience a functional map of the whole system.

mechanics.function: Using an apparent contradiction as a teaching hinge
mechanics.mechanic: Present an observation that seems inconsistent, explain why a simple model cannot account for it, and use that tension to motivate a more nuanced model with multiple pathways or components.
mechanics.when_to_use: Use when the audience may encounter conflicting outcomes or oversimplified explanations.
mechanics.avoid: Do not manufacture a paradox; distinguish genuinely different conditions, populations, or mechanisms.

mechanics.function: Translating evidence into a causal chain
mechanics.mechanic: Move explicitly from intervention or input, to intermediate signal, to system-level response, and finally to the observable outcome. Label the links so readers can see which steps are established and which are inferred.
mechanics.when_to_use: Use when explaining why a behavior, environmental condition, or treatment might produce an effect.
mechanics.avoid: Do not collapse correlation, mechanism, and outcome into a single claim.

mechanics.function: Separating normal regulation from extreme manipulation
mechanics.mechanic: Contrast ordinary physiological or operational levels with unusually strong interventions. Explain that an effect observed under extreme conditions may not predict the result, safety, or usefulness of normal-range modulation.
mechanics.when_to_use: Use when discussing drugs, supplements, experimental tools, optimization practices, or high-intensity interventions.
mechanics.avoid: Do not let a warning become an implicit endorsement or treat extreme findings as routine recommendations.

mechanics.mechanic: After presenting a general pattern, identify an important exception, explain why it follows a different mechanism, and state the boundary conditions under which the general advice should not be applied.
mechanics.when_to_use: Use whenever individual variation, medical conditions, technical constraints, or competing goals could change the recommendation.
mechanics.avoid: Do not bury the exception after presenting the advice as universally applicable.

mechanics.function: Converting timing into an adaptable protocol
mechanics.mechanic: Explain how repeated schedules or feedback loops can reinforce a response, then offer a gradual adjustment strategy rather than only a binary change. Include an alternative for people whose constraints require a different pattern.
mechanics.when_to_use: Use for habit formation, training, scheduling, behavior change, or systems with adaptation over time.
mechanics.avoid: Do not present a precise schedule as universally optimal; identify it as a starting framework that may require adjustment.

mechanics.function: Closing with a compact integration and callback
mechanics.mechanic: After several mechanisms have been introduced, restate each as a functional role—such as accelerator, brake, signal, or threshold—and connect the summary back to the original practical objective.
mechanics.when_to_use: Use at the end of a dense section or before moving to the next subsystem.
mechanics.avoid: Do not merely repeat terminology; summarize relationships and decisions the audience can now understand.
